decisions.decision: Retain permitted detached-free writer behavior; record D48 stale source rationale without editing production, ledger or historical ADR. T91 adds a valid reader regression.
decisions.normative_basis: Effective §7.5.4 after Issue #147 says the two subsection-header integers are non-negative and strikes NOTE 3's prior statement that update subsections can never start with zero. §7.5.4 requires entry 0 always be free with generation 65 535; the linked-list head points to a free object and tail returns to object 0. The second mechanism permits a deleted entry pointing to 0 with generation 65 535 outside that list. §7.5.6 requires a deletion to remain in file bytes and be marked by the updated cross-reference entries.
decisions.current_evidence: read_classic_table parses subsection first as u32, so 0 is representable. incremental_update_freeing continues to emit detached free entries and does not rewrite entry 0; that remains a choice, but its doc comment quotes the struck NOTE 3 as the reason. Existing a_freed_object_is_gone_to_the_reader_and_still_in_the_file verifies the detached mechanism, not an object-zero subsection.
decisions.scope: One test PASS, covering linked object0 update and detached control; all-targets syntax Clippy PASS. Does not require writers to choose the linked mechanism or certify every free list.
decisions.draft: crates/pdf-syntax/tests/incremental_object_zero_spec_audit.rs builds a valid base PDF with page /Resources and object 5 in use, confirms its xref and object-zero entry without recovery, then hand-appends an exact-offset classic section deleting object 5. Target subsection 0 1 makes 0→5 and subsection 5 1 makes 5→0 at generation 1; the positive control uses the allowed detached mechanism with 5→0 at generation 65 535. /ID is omitted as an optional entry. It checks the old object is inaccessible, both stated sections are present, the /Prev chain is not cut, the catalog remains available, and no recovery occurred.

decisions.decision: No open/read-time defect. Record the change in signing-time digest constraints and keep the current no-signing boundary explicit.
decisions.basis: §12.7.5.5 says seed-value constraints are used at the time a signature is applied; §12.8.3.4 separately says seed values are not validation constraints. The erratum replaces a key-specific digest note with a general rule when a mechanism mandates its own digest.

decisions.decision: No reader gap from not implementing acceptable DigestMethod selection/order while there is no signing consumer. Do not imply that parsing seed values implements the changed signing policy.
